transcript:
Fireflies.ai Transcript

Meeting: Marketplace listing copy review (AWS + GCP) - internal
Recorded: Jan 22, 2025 9:00 AM PT
Duration: 42 min
Attendees:
- Soojin Lee (Product Marketing)
- Camila Reyes (Marketing)
- Ben Carter (Growth Marketing)
- Connor O'Brien (Release Eng / launch coordination)
- Elliot Price (Docs)

---
Summary (auto-generated)
The team reviewed draft AWS and GCP Marketplace listing copy for Redwood Inference. Main edits: tighten the headline, clarify deployment modes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private), avoid over-claiming on security/compliance, and ensure the copy matches the onboarding flow (purchase → entitlement → org linking). Screenshot set needs to show the onboarding wizard, entitlement status, and usage/cost views. Next steps assigned for copy edits, keywords, links, and confirming submission requirements.

Topics
- Headline + positioning for marketplace buyers
- SKU naming consistency (Hosted/Dedicated/Private + add-ons)
- Security language (SOC 2 / encryption / audit logs)
- Onboarding steps and what to show in screenshots
- Keywords + attribution (UTMs)

Action items (auto-generated)
- Soojin: revise AWS headline + opening block; add SKU callout
- Ben: finalize keywords + remove risky competitor keywords
- Elliot: confirm links + security wording alignment
- Connor: confirm screenshot requirements + submission timeline
- Camila: final approval of updated drafts

Questions (captured)
- Do we need separate listings for Dedicated vs Private in GCP or can it be a single solution with multiple plans?
- Are we allowed to say “data residency” or should we say “regional deployment options”?
- Can we mention KMS generically or must we say “customer-managed keys (where supported)”?

---

[00:00] Soojin Lee: Alright. Thanks all. Goal today is quick pass on the marketplace copy drafts, AWS and GCP. We want to tighten the first screen, make sure we’re not saying anything Security will hate, and line up with the onboarding flow.

[00:18] Camila Reyes: And, just as context, partner teams are moving faster than usual. So we need something we can submit and iterate on, not like perfect literature.

[00:28] Ben Carter: Yep. Also we should make sure the keywords aren’t… weird. AWS rejects for stuff that looks like competitor targeting sometimes.

[00:36] Connor O'Brien: I’m mostly here to keep us honest on what screenshots and required fields we need by Friday. The partner portal has those annoying “must include” checkboxes.

[00:46] Elliot Price: And I’ll sanity check any doc links. Right now in the draft I saw “link TBD” like four times.

[00:55] Soojin Lee: Cool. Starting with AWS. Current headline says, “Run open LLMs with low latency and predictable cost.” I think it’s fine but it might be too generic.

[01:07] Camila Reyes: It reads like every inference vendor. What’s the Redwood hook? “Production-grade inference across hosted, dedicated, private” — something like that.

[01:17] Soojin Lee: Yeah. I had an alternate: “High-performance LLM inference across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.” Little long.

[01:26] Ben Carter: AWS marketplace buyers are procurement-ish. They want: can I buy it, can I control spend, does it have an SLA, can I deploy in my region. So the headline should maybe signal “enterprise ready” without sounding like, I don’t know, a bank.

[01:43] Camila Reyes: Right. Developer-first but not developer-only.

[01:47] Connor O'Brien: Also AWS character limits are strict. There’s like headline vs short description vs long description.

[01:53] Soojin Lee: Okay. Then the first paragraph right now: “Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform for running and optimizing LLM inference.” That’s the company one-liner. Should we lead with the marketplace angle? Like, “Purchase through AWS Marketplace to apply committed spend.”

[02:10] Ben Carter: Mention committed spend, yes. But not in the first sentence maybe. First sentence should be value. Second sentence: procurement / billing.

[02:18] Elliot Price: And then we should link to the “Buying via marketplace” FAQ. We’re drafting it but we’ll have a docs page.

[02:26] Camila Reyes: Also we keep saying “Hosted API” and then “Dedicated capacity” and then “Private deployment.” In AWS listing, we should use consistent nouns. Like “Redwood Hosted”, “Redwood Dedicated”, “Redwood Private”. Otherwise buyers are confused.

[02:41] Soojin Lee: Good catch. In the copy I used both “Dedicated” and “Reserved capacity” interchangeably. I’ll normalize.

[02:49] Connor O'Brien: Please do. Engineering is using “entitlement IDs” that match those names. So if the listing says “Reserved” but the console says “Dedicated,” it’s a support ticket factory.

[03:02] Soojin Lee: Next: the bullets. We currently have:
- “Faster tokens with optimized kernels”
- “Simple REST and SDKs”
- “SOC 2 compliant”
- “Supports VPC and on-prem”

[03:16] Elliot Price: The “SOC 2 compliant” phrase. We should not. We should say “SOC 2 Type II report available” or “audited controls.” The FAQ draft has specific language.

[03:27] Camila Reyes: Yeah, “compliant” is a red flag and also not precise. Let’s not.

[03:33] Ben Carter: Plus AWS reviewers sometimes ask for evidence when you say that.

[03:37] Soojin Lee: Okay, swapping that bullet. Maybe “Security and compliance: encryption in transit/at rest, audit logs, SSO/SAML (plan-dependent).”

[03:48] Elliot Price: Careful on “at rest.” We do have at rest encryption, but wording should be “encrypted at rest in supported storage layers” or something. But that’s too legal-y.

[03:57] Connor O'Brien: The security packet has the exact phrasing Marcus wanted. Use that.

[04:02] Soojin Lee: Got it, I’ll align with packet language.

[04:06] Camila Reyes: Also “Supports VPC and on-prem” — is that accurate for marketplace? On AWS Marketplace we’re primarily selling… what exactly? Hosted API credits? Or private deployment in their VPC?

[04:18] Connor O'Brien: For AWS we have SKUs for Hosted and Dedicated, plus Private as a separate plan. The “Private” can be VPC. On-prem is more of a separate motion. I’d avoid “on-prem” in the marketplace listing unless we want reviewer questions.

[04:34] Soojin Lee: Okay, change to “Private deployment in your VPC (where applicable)” and then mention on-prem via sales contact.

[04:43] Ben Carter: Yeah, marketplace listing is not the place to promise air-gapped installs.

[04:49] Elliot Price: We can add a “Contact Sales for on-prem / regulated environments” line.

[04:55] Soojin Lee: Next: the “How it works” section. I wrote “continuous batching, KV cache, smart routing.” That’s very engineer-y.

[05:04] Camila Reyes: That’s fine lower in the page. But up top, we should say outcomes: lower latency, predictable throughput, cost controls.

[05:13] Ben Carter: Also avoid “smart routing” sounding like we route customer data randomly. Just phrase it as “policy-based routing” and mention regions.

[05:23] Soojin Lee: Ha, true. “Smart” makes it sound like magic.

[05:28] Connor O'Brien: And for GCP, they care about “deployment steps” section. It’s more prescriptive: click deploy, link org, etc.

[05:36] Soojin Lee: We’ll get to GCP. Staying on AWS: keywords. Ben, what do we have now?

[05:43] Ben Carter: Draft has: “LLM inference, GPT, Claude, Bedrock alternative, embeddings, rerank, vector, GPU, latency, SOC2, HIPAA.” Some of those we should remove. Competitor brand names (“Claude”) I’d avoid. “HIPAA” is a no unless we have explicit program language.

[06:03] Camila Reyes: Yep, do not put HIPAA in keywords.

[06:06] Soojin Lee: Agree. Also “GPT” is a trademark-y thing.

[06:10] Ben Carter: So we’ll keep generic: “LLM inference, text generation, chat API, embeddings, reranking, GPU inference, low latency, dedicated GPU, private VPC, audit logs, SSO, SAML.”

[06:26] Elliot Price: “Audit logs” is okay, we do have audit logs. But if we say it, the docs link should explain what is audited and retention.

[06:34] Soojin Lee: Noted.

[06:37] Connor O'Brien: Screenshot plan: AWS requires at least one architecture-ish image sometimes, plus product UI. Our inventory doc suggests: (1) Console model/route dashboard, (2) onboarding wizard showing “Link your AWS purchase,” (3) usage/cost breakdown.

[06:55] Camila Reyes: I want a screenshot that screams “enterprise ready”: like org settings with SSO toggle, audit log view, something.

[07:03] Elliot Price: We need to be careful. If SSO is plan-dependent we can show it but caption it, like “available on enterprise plans.”

[07:11] Soojin Lee: And also avoid leaking customer names in screenshots. Make sure it’s a demo org.

[07:16] Connor O'Brien: Design is doing redaction pass, but we need to specify which pages. If we try to show too many, we’ll miss the deadline.

[07:25] Ben Carter: Also the first screenshot in AWS listing tends to show in the search results preview. We should pick the best one.

[07:33] Camila Reyes: The cost dashboard is compelling. It differentiates us vs “here’s an endpoint.”

[07:39] Soojin Lee: Okay. Let’s decide screenshot set: 3 screenshots, plus 1 diagram max. Priority: onboarding wizard, usage/cost dashboard, model/route performance dashboard. Optional: security settings.

[07:55] Elliot Price: If we do security settings, we need to confirm the UI is stable. I’ve seen it change.

[08:01] Connor O'Brien: Yeah, it changed in the last PR.

[08:04] Soojin Lee: Let’s skip security settings screenshot for now.

[08:08] Camila Reyes: Fine. We can cover that in the security packet / FAQ.

[08:13] Soojin Lee: Moving to the long description section on AWS: I want to add a “Choose your deployment” block with three bullets: Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, Private (VPC). Then a “Common use cases” block.

[08:28] Ben Carter: Use cases: “customer support automation,” “search/rerank,” “agentic workflows,” “internal copilots.” But keep it not too hype-y.

[08:37] Camila Reyes: Add “regulated workloads” but again no HIPAA.

[08:42] Elliot Price: Maybe phrase as “workloads requiring stricter security controls.”

[08:47] Soojin Lee: Yep.

[08:50] Connor O'Brien: Also AWS wants “Support information” and “Refund policy.” We need a standard line. Do we have one?

[08:57] Elliot Price: Docs team can provide standard support contact. Refund policy depends on marketplace terms; Finance/Legal usually wants “per AWS Marketplace terms.”

[09:08] Camila Reyes: Put minimal.

[09:11] Soojin Lee: Great.

[09:13] (crosstalk)

[09:14] Soojin Lee: Okay GCP draft. GCP listing format is weird: “Solution overview” + “Deploy” steps. The draft currently says, “Deploy Redwood Inference and connect to your models.” That’s not correct because we’re not deploying a container via click-to-deploy in all cases.

[09:32] Connor O'Brien: Right, for GCP marketplace we’re doing a SaaS listing. So the deploy step is basically “Buy plan, then log into Redwood Console, link org.”

[09:42] Elliot Price: We need to be super explicit there: “After purchase, you will receive an entitlement. In the Redwood Console, link your GCP billing account / org.”

[09:51] Ben Carter: And “region selection” needs to be explained. People get stuck if they buy in one region and try to provision in another.

[10:01] Soojin Lee: Yeah, we’ve seen region mismatch support tickets already.

[10:06] Camila Reyes: Let’s put a short “Before you begin” section: have a Redwood account, admin permissions, know your target region.

[10:15] Elliot Price: Exactly. The docs page will have the full steps, but listing should not be vague.

[10:22] Soojin Lee: Copy tone: On GCP draft, I used “enterprise-grade” a lot. Probably too much.

[10:29] Camila Reyes: Use it once maybe. Otherwise it becomes noise.

[10:33] Ben Carter: Also, GCP reviewers are picky about “security claims.” If you say “data residency guaranteed,” they’ll ask “which regions.” Better say “regional deployment options; contact us for availability.”

[10:48] Soojin Lee: Noted. We should not invent region list.

[10:51] Connor O'Brien: We can reference “supported regions displayed in Console.” That’s accurate.

[10:57] Soojin Lee: Good.

[11:00] Elliot Price: For encryption: avoid “customer-managed keys” unless it’s specifically supported in that plan. The security FAQ says “KMS integrations available for Private deployments” I think.

[11:11] Soojin Lee: I’ll mirror that.

[11:14] Camila Reyes: Quick competitor mention question: do we mention “Bedrock alternative” anywhere?

[11:19] Ben Carter: No. Not in listing. Too risky.

[11:22] Soojin Lee: Agree.

[11:24] Camila Reyes: Okay.

[11:26] Soojin Lee: Let’s talk about the “Why buy via marketplace” section. I want two bullets: apply cloud commit, single invoice.

[11:34] Ben Carter: And “streamlined vendor onboarding.” That’s a huge one. Procurement likes it.

[11:40] Connor O'Brien: But keep it accurate; it helps with procurement but there’s still security review.

[11:45] Soojin Lee: Yep.

[11:47] Elliot Price: We also should include “Support” and “SLA” messaging carefully. “Premium SLA available” is fine, but don’t state specific numbers unless legal approved.

[11:56] Soojin Lee: In the draft I wrote “99.9 uptime.” I’ll remove.

[12:01] Camila Reyes: Yes remove, unless we have standard public SLA doc.

[12:05] Soojin Lee: Okay.

[12:07] Ben Carter: Keywords for GCP: similar set. Also GCP search is more forgiving but still: no competitor names.

[12:16] Connor O'Brien: On screenshots: GCP listing usually wants less marketing screenshots, more “what user sees after clicking deploy.” But since it’s SaaS, we can show the onboarding wizard again.

[12:28] Elliot Price: And a step-by-step text block: “1) Purchase, 2) Create Redwood org, 3) Link entitlement, 4) Generate API key.”

[12:38] Soojin Lee: Okay. Then the FAQ section. Right now we have Qs like “Can Redwood see my prompts” and “Do you store data.” We need exact answers.

[12:48] Elliot Price: We can say “Data handling depends on product and customer configuration.” But that’s too vague. The Security FAQ has “Prompts and outputs are processed to provide the service; retention controlled per plan; logs may include metadata; see FAQ.”

[13:05] Camila Reyes: Keep it human.

[13:07] Soojin Lee: Yeah. “We don’t train on your data by default” — can we say that?

[13:12] Elliot Price: We need to confirm. I think that’s in the standard statement, but I’d rather copy it verbatim from the approved security FAQ.

[13:20] Connor O'Brien: Security sign-off is required before submission anyway.

[13:25] Ben Carter: And avoid saying “never”.

[13:28] Soojin Lee: Okay.

[13:30] (brief silence)

[13:32] Soojin Lee: Let’s jump to the opening copy edit decisions. Camila, what do you want the top to say?

[13:38] Camila Reyes: Something like: “Redwood Inference helps engineering teams run LLM inference with predictable latency, cost, and reliability—available via AWS and Google Cloud marketplaces for streamlined procurement.” That’s one sentence. Then second: “Choose Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, or Private deployment.”

[13:56] Soojin Lee: That’s good. I’ll do that.

[13:59] Ben Carter: And then a third line: “Start in minutes, scale to enterprise.”

[14:04] Camila Reyes: Sure, but careful, “minutes” might be questioned if entitlement takes time.

[14:10] Connor O'Brien: Exactly. Entitlements can lag. Maybe “Get started quickly.”

[14:14] Soojin Lee: “Get started quickly” it is.

[14:17] Elliot Price: Also include a line: “If your entitlement hasn’t appeared in the Console within X minutes, contact support.” But maybe not in listing.

[14:25] Soojin Lee: Better in docs.

[14:27] Connor O'Brien: Yes.

[14:30] Soojin Lee: Okay. SKU section: We should have consistent names and a note that add-ons like “Compliance/Retention” and “Premium SLA” may be separate line items.

[14:42] Camila Reyes: How do we say that without turning it into a pricing table?

[14:46] Soojin Lee: “Optional add-ons available (compliance package, extended observability retention, premium support/SLA).”

[14:54] Ben Carter: That helps with enterprise buyers. They want to know the compliance story exists.

[14:59] Elliot Price: But again, don’t imply a specific certification. “Compliance package” is vague enough.

[15:04] Soojin Lee: Understood.

[15:06] Connor O'Brien: Can we also include in listing the support path: “Open a ticket in Console” and an email?

[15:13] Elliot Price: Listing usually wants an email. Console ticketing is for customers already provisioned.

[15:18] Soojin Lee: Okay.

[15:20] Ben Carter: Attribution note: When we link to docs from listing, we should use UTMs so we can track marketplace traffic separately. Even if the marketplace itself has reporting, we need our own.

[15:31] Camila Reyes: Yes. Ben, do your thing.

[15:34] Ben Carter: I’ll add UTMs for “aws_marketplace” and “gcp_marketplace” and “listing” as campaign, something like that.

[15:43] Soojin Lee: Great.

[15:45] Camila Reyes: Another copy nit: we keep saying “open models” only. But we support some proprietary? Or no.

[15:51] Soojin Lee: Mostly open models in catalog. We shouldn’t promise “any model.” We can say “curated model catalog” and “bring-your-own model available on Private” maybe.

[16:02] Connor O'Brien: “Bring your own” is not marketplace self-serve though. But Private deployments can support custom model onboarding.

[16:10] Elliot Price: Phrase: “Support for custom model onboarding available for Private deployments (contact us).”

[16:16] Soojin Lee: Works.

[16:18] Camila Reyes: And leave it at that.

[16:21] Soojin Lee: Okay we’re at ~16 minutes in the transcript; skipping ahead to the security claims section.

[16:27] Soojin Lee: Current FAQ answer: “All data is encrypted and we have full audit logging.” That’s too absolute.

[16:34] Elliot Price: Yep. We need “Encryption in transit (TLS) and encryption at rest in supported systems.” And “Audit logs available for admin actions; retention depends on plan.” Something like that.

[16:47] Ben Carter: The phrase “full audit logging” will get flagged.

[16:50] Camila Reyes: Also avoid saying “zero data retention.” Not true.

[16:54] Soojin Lee: I’ll rewrite using the approved phrasing.

[16:59] Connor O'Brien: Another point: “SSO/SAML.” That is real but enterprise-only. Add “available on enterprise tiers.”

[17:07] Soojin Lee: Got it.

[17:09] (crosstalk)

[17:10] Camila Reyes: The “differentiators” block: I want to keep “production economics” language. That’s our positioning.

[17:16] Soojin Lee: Agreed. I’ll put: “Optimize cost per token with caching, batching, and routing controls.”

[17:24] Ben Carter: That’s a strong line.

[17:27] Elliot Price: Just don’t go too deep on “KV cache.” It’s not a listing audience term.

[17:33] Soojin Lee: Right.

[17:35] Connor O'Brien: Also on AWS listing there’s a section “Support and training” sometimes. We can mention “docs, SDKs, Solutions Engineering for enterprise.”

[17:45] Camila Reyes: Mention Solutions Engineering, yes.

[17:48] Soojin Lee: Okay.

[17:50] Ben Carter: Are we including pricing numbers in listing copy?

[17:54] Soojin Lee: No. We’ll rely on marketplace pricing table.

[17:58] Camila Reyes: Good.

[18:00] Connor O'Brien: Timeline: we need updated copy in the doc by end of day tomorrow so Partnerships can submit Friday morning. If we miss Friday, we slip a week.

[18:11] Soojin Lee: I can do copy edits by tomorrow morning. I’ll post in the shared drive.

[18:16] Elliot Price: I can add links today, but I need final slug names. Are the docs pages final path “/docs/marketplace/aws” or “/docs/buy/aws-marketplace”?

[18:26] Connor O'Brien: Not sure. Elliot, can you just put placeholders with a note?

[18:30] Elliot Price: I’d rather pick one consistent path. I’ll coordinate with Docs team, but for now I can put “redwoodinference.com/docs/marketplace/aws” and we can redirect.

[18:41] Soojin Lee: That works.

[18:43] Ben Carter: If you do that, I can also add UTMs now.

[18:47] Elliot Price: Great.

[18:50] Camila Reyes: Another point: GCP listing tends to want “Privacy policy URL” and “Terms.” Do we have those ready?

[18:58] Elliot Price: Yes, legal pages exist. I’ll include.

[19:02] Connor O'Brien: Cool.

[19:04] Soojin Lee: Let’s do a quick read of the revised opening paragraph we want. I’ll draft live:
“Redwood Inference helps engineering teams run LLM inference with predictable latency, cost, and reliability. Purchase via AWS Marketplace or Google Cloud Marketplace to streamline procurement and apply committed cloud spend. Choose from Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, or Private deployment options.”

[19:28] Camila Reyes: That’s solid.

[19:30] Ben Carter: Yep.

[19:31] Elliot Price: Replace “apply committed cloud spend” with “apply existing cloud commitments” maybe. Less finance-y.

[19:39] Soojin Lee: Okay.

[19:41] Connor O'Brien: And ensure we’re not implying it works for all cloud commits. But generally it does.

[19:46] Soojin Lee: Fine.

[19:48] (minor audio glitch)

[19:50] Soojin Lee: Anything else? Keywords. Ben, you’ll post final list?

[19:55] Ben Carter: Yes. I’ll do two lists, AWS and GCP. Probably same but AWS has a limit.

[20:03] Camila Reyes: Please remove “SOC2” from keywords. Put it in body copy if needed, but I’d rather not as keyword.

[20:10] Ben Carter: Agreed.

[20:12] Soojin Lee: Screenshot owners: Connor, are you coordinating with Design?

[20:17] Connor O'Brien: Yeah. I’ll ping design ticket. We need: onboarding wizard screenshot showing entitlement state, usage dashboard, performance dashboard. Possibly a simple diagram.

[20:31] Soojin Lee: If diagram is too slow, we can drop it.

[20:35] Camila Reyes: Drop diagram. Use product UI.

[20:39] Connor O'Brien: Works.

[20:41] Elliot Price: Just remind them to use demo org and not production data.

[20:46] Connor O'Brien: Will do.

[20:48] Soojin Lee: Okay last item: “Do/don’t” language. We should avoid: “guaranteed,” “fully,” “compliant,” “zero retention.” We should say: “available,” “configurable,” “plan-dependent,” “report available under NDA.”

[21:10] Camila Reyes: Exactly.

[21:12] Ben Carter: One more nuance: “data residency.” Avoid as a claim, say “regional deployment options” and “contact us for region availability.”

[21:22] Soojin Lee: Yep.

[21:24] Elliot Price: Also include “Shared responsibility model” line somewhere? Or too much?

[21:30] Camila Reyes: Probably too much in listing. Keep that in security packet.

[21:35] Soojin Lee: Agree.

[21:37] Connor O'Brien: Alright I’ll send a quick follow-up with deadlines.

[21:41] Soojin Lee: Thanks. I’ll summarize action items now.

[21:45] Soojin Lee: So: I’ll update AWS headline + first two paragraphs and SKU block by tomorrow. Ben final keywords by tomorrow. Elliot links today/tomorrow. Connor confirms screenshot requirements and timelines. Camila final approval Friday.

[22:03] Camila Reyes: Perfect.

[22:04] Ben Carter: Sounds good.

[22:06] Elliot Price: Yep.

[22:07] Connor O'Brien: Great.

[22:10] Soojin Lee: Ending here. Thanks all.

(Transcript ends — remainder of recording is mostly silence / calendar chatter; Fireflies cut off)
